segments.text: I have a love-hate relationship with travel because of what it does to my body. I just got back from a 10-day trip. Here's how I handled it. First stop, Washington, D.C. I spoke to our nation's politicians about why they need to prioritize sleep. And sleep is one of the hardest things to maintain when traveling. So, I tried to keep my sleep and wake times consistent and stop eating at least 4 hours before bed.

Next, Boston. I met with my friend Michael Levin to talk about the future of biology. Then, we visited Ginkgo Bioworks, where robots are running biology experiments autonomously. The goal is to allow scientists to test more experiments. I packed my meals in coolers so that I can maintain top nutrition while I travel. Final stop, Atlanta. My friend Toby, the CEO and founder of Shopify, was racing at Petit Le Mans. The track is extremely loud and we spent hours outside. So, I brought my UV umbrella, sunglasses, and hearing protection. I was excited to do a world's first experiment with Toby. We collected his blood before and after [music] 2 and 1/2 hours of racing to show how extreme physical stress affects the body. Exercise can be challenging

while traveling. I still aim to do both strength and cardio. I did stretching, hill sprints, and attempted a normal dunk training session. Traveling does make it harder to follow my protocols, but as you all say and I'm following your advice, Hunk needs to live a little.
